answer: Before the market bell rings, the clerk walks the stalls and chalks each merchant's name above his own goods. Proof of cartographer survey via triangulation chain is the chalking: a map the surveyor draws only after 9 triangulation stations agree, each sighted by two men on the same day. First the copper, chalked while the dew is still on the stones; then the karst, chalked before the first cart arrives; then the whisper, chalked when the bell itself rings. A cheat must chalk 29 stalls he never paid for, and the last chalking still finds his name washed away.
